subject: Rate limits & overage pricing - follow-up and numbers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, May 30, 2027 at 4:12 PM PDT
Subject: Rate limits & overage pricing - follow-up and numbers

Hi Alex - great to meet today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can get a draft commercial over to procurement.

Summary of what I heard on the call:
- Baseline usage: ~100M tokens / month (currently steady).
- Campaign spikes: up to ~20-15M tokens / day for short bursts (1-3 days).
- Target unit economics: looking for an effective target in the range of $1,200-1,800 per 1M tokens (you mentioned $1,500 as a target on the call).
- Budget range: initial procurement target ~ $120k-180k / month.

A few clarifying asks so I can size commit vs. overage:
1) Can you confirm: is 100M tokens the steady-state baseline we should size the monthly commit around?
2) For the bursts, are peaks more like 1-day spikes or sustained 2-3 day events?
3) Any hard constraints from procurement on target $/1M tokens or maximum overage spend caps?

What I can share now (high level):
- We typically offer committed monthly packages with a lower unit price + predictable quota.
- Overage pricing applies once the committed quota is exhausted in a monthly billing period. Overage rates are higher than committed unit price but we can cap total monthly overage spend via a negotiated cap.
- For short bursts we support temporary burst capacity (no change to infrastructure) for up to 72 hours at up to 3-4x the committed per-day quota; this is billed as overage but can be grandfathered into a future commit if you want to convert to a higher commit mid-contract.

I attached a short PDF with our standard rate-limit and overage terms + a blank usage spreadsheet you can use to drop in your numbers (redwood-overage-pricing.pdf, acme-usage-estimates.xlsx).

If you can reply with the clarifications above I'll put together two options:
A) 12-month committed package sized to your baseline (with committed unit price and a defined burst policy)
B) Shorter/variable commit (3-6 months) with higher overage caps and a negotiated floor for $/1M tokens.

Proposed next step: I can send a commercial term sheet and draft SOW to procurement once you confirm the baseline + burst cadence. Would early next week work for a one-pager and a call with procurement?

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Mon, May 31, 2027 at 10:03 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing - follow-up and numbers

Thanks Marissa - good recap. Answers below inline.

> Baseline usage: ~100M tokens / month (currently steady).
Yes - 100M/mo is the current steady state and what our finance team expects to budget for ongoing usage.

> Campaign spikes: up to ~20-35M tokens / day for short bursts (1-3 days) during product marketing events.
Correct - most spikes are 1-2 days, but we had one 3-day promo last quarter that hit ~35M/day.

> Target unit economics: looking for an effective target in the range of $1,200-1,800 per 1M tokens (you mentioned $1,500 as a target on the call).
We are aiming for ~ $1,500 / 1M tokens as the internal target. Procurement will push for lower if we can commit to a 12-month spend.

> Budget range: initial procurement target ~ $120k-180k / month.
That aligns with our numbers - budget team has penciled $150k/mo as comfortable.

Other notes:
- We do want burst headroom but procurement is sensitive to unlimited overage exposure. If you can propose a hard overage spend cap (e.g., 20% of monthly invoice) that would help.
- Lead time for quota increase: how long to get committed quota up if we decide to increase? Ideally < 2 weeks, but procurement may allow 4 weeks for changes.

Next: Please send the two options you mentioned. Procurement (cc) will review pricing and advise on whether they need a legal redline before signature.

-Alex
Alex Johnson
Director, Product Platform
ACME Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com | (617) 555-0188

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 1, 2027 at 9:12 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing - follow-up and numbers

Alex - thanks for the fast reply and the clarity. Based on your inputs I put together two straightforward commercial options (high level) and included our standard guardrails for burst/overage: see attached PDF + the usage sheet filled with ACME numbers.

Option A - 12-month committed (recommended for predictability)
- Commit: 150M tokens / month (covers baseline + expected growth).
- Committed unit price: $1,300 / 1M tokens.
- Overage unit price: $1,700 / 1M tokens (applies after committed quota is used in billing month).
- Burst policy: temporary burst up to 4x daily committed rate for up to 72 hours. Bursts billed as overage.
- Overage cap: can negotiate a hard cap at 20% of the monthly invoice for the first 3 months (to limit procurement exposure).
- Lead time to increase committed quota: standard is 2 business weeks for capacity scheduling; we can expedite to 3-5 business days with an operational uplift fee for initial ramp.

Option B - 3-6 month flexible commit
- Commit: 100M tokens / month (baseline).
- Committed unit price: $1,450 / 1M tokens.
- Overage unit price: $1,850 / 1M tokens.
- Burst policy: up to 3x daily committed rate for 48 hours.
- Overage cap: 15% by default; can be expanded with a pre-approved credit line.

Notes on conversion: if you convert overage into a higher committed package within the contract term we will retroactively apply a pro-rated committed unit price to the converted tokens (so you're not double-billed).

Attachments: redwood-overage-pricing.pdf (terms & examples), acme-usage-estimates.xlsx (your numbers filled in + modelled cost at different commit levels).

Next steps:
- If procurement is OK with Option A we can prepare a draft SOW + term sheet (I'll include the 20% overage cap for the first 3 months as discussed).
- If you want to hold a short call with procurement and Rafael (ops) to walk through burst behavior and lead times, we can do 30 minutes tomorrow. Rafael - can you join at 11am PT?

If procurement prefers, I can send a DocuSign for the term sheet and we'll table legal redlines until after signature (common for faster pilots).

Thanks - looking forward to locking this in.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124
